arguments.summary: Fixed-evidence draft: the supplied grids provide conditional earnings/multiple sensitivities, but no valuation conclusion or relative preference is supportable. NVDA has the stronger 63-session tape and a guided AI-infrastructure bridge; MU has a nearer Q4 earnings test and much higher realized volatility; QQQ diversifies issuer events but retains dated exposure to both.

claims.text: NVDA reported H1 FY27 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.85 and guided Q3 revenue of $108bn ±2%, 74% GAAP gross margin ±50bp, assuming no China Data Center compute revenue. The assumed FY27 $8/$10/$12 EPS cases leave constant-share Q3+Q4 residuals of $3.15/$5.15/$7.15. The associated 20x/25x/30x P/E inputs are assumptions, not observed multiples, fair values, consensus or probabilities.

At the 2026-09-18 split-adjusted close, NVDA's assumed bear/base/bull grid gives -28.02%/+12.48%/+61.97% sensitivities; base breaks even at 22.227x on $10 assumed EPS or $8.8908 assumed EPS at 25x. NVDA returned 5.50% over 63 sessions, 8.08 percentage points ahead of QQQ, while its 63-session realized volatility was 39.63% versus QQQ's 20.85%.

MU reported nine-month FY26 GAAP diluted EPS of $41.40 and guided Q4 GAAP EPS of $30.73 ±$1.00. Assumed $65/$72/$78 annual EPS cases imply constant-share Q4 residuals of $23.60/$30.60/$36.60: base approximately completes guidance; bear tests weaker memory demand/pricing or margin; bull requires above-guidance AI-memory results. The 10x/14x/18x P/E inputs are assumptions.

At the 2026-09-18 split-adjusted close, MU's assumed bear/base/bull grid gives -36.01%/-0.77%/+38.22% sensitivities; base breaks even at 14.1083x on $72 assumed EPS or $72.5571 assumed EPS at 14x. MU's -10.42% 63-session return lagged QQQ by 7.83 points and its 89.56% realized volatility exceeded NVDA and QQQ.

QQQ's sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08 as of 2026-08-31. Dated 2026-09-18 holdings included NVDA at 8.535228% and MU at 5.012336%, 13.547564% combined before other semiconductor holdings. The aggregate ETF metric cannot validate or be directly ranked against assumed corporate scenario P/Es.

NVIDIA guidance excludes China Data Center compute revenue and its filing identifies export-control barriers and Taiwan/South Korea supply dependence. Micron discloses unquantified trade, tariff, equipment/component and raw-material risks. QQQ transmits issuer shocks through dated holdings, but supplied evidence does not quantify comparable financial exposure or fund-wide sensitivity.

NVDA's stronger 63-session performance and lower realized volatility than MU coincide with a base case requiring guided Q3 execution plus Q4 continuation; MU's base is more immediately testable but has little selected-multiple cushion. QQQ is broader but directly exposed to both. This describes different risk structures, not a preference, because valuation comparability, macro regime and policy magnitudes are missing.

gaps.description: No issuer multiple history, forward earnings/consensus, or comparable corporate valuation methodology is supplied. This prevents determining whether scenario P/E bands are fair, normal or attractive versus QQQ's aggregate sponsor metric; it blocks valuation conclusions and unconditional relative preference, but not conditional grid arithmetic.
No dated yield/inflation/credit-spread observation paired with customer order or capex evidence is supplied. The prevailing macro regime and a macro-adjusted relative preference cannot be identified.

Current policy applicability and quantified issuer exposure are absent: NVIDIA license/product applicability and Micron geography/product/input sensitivity are unverified. This blocks policy-loss estimates and policy-based ranking.

assumptions: All grid EPS and P/E values are analyst assumptions, not consensus, observed multiples, fair values, probabilities or forecasts.
Residual EPS uses a constant diluted-share approximation; company fiscal periods exceed the 63-session horizon.
QQQ holdings and valuation are dated sponsor reporting, not current holdings; fund and corporate P/E bases are non-equivalent.
arguments.counter_thesis: AI infrastructure and memory demand could exceed guidance, while multiple compression could still offset operating delivery. QQQ diversification reduces issuer-event concentration but not correlated AI/semiconductor exposure.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA after next results: revenue, margin or outlook below the guided-Q3-plus-Q4-residual mechanism weakens the base grid; sustained ramp evidence and Q4 support weaken the bear mechanism.
Review MU at fiscal Q4 results: a material miss to $30.73 ±$1.00 guidance or the $30.60 base residual weakens the base mechanism; delivery with sustained margin/outlook supports it.
Refresh QQQ sponsor holdings and aggregate valuation: changed NVDA/MU weights or aggregate P/E changes the dated look-through comparison.

NVDA.counter_thesis: Demand/mix or margin deceleration, export/supply disruption, or multiple compression can defeat the bridge.
